newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu associates also under indictment shadow.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu associates also under indictment shadow.

text.p: Israeli police dropped a bombshell this week when they recommended Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and three associates be tried in an influence peddling scandal.
The three, who like the Israeli leader claim innocence, are:

JUSTICE MINISTER TZACHI HANEGBI, 40, a key Netanyahu Likud party ally, became Israel's top law man in November 1996 when Netanyahu's first justice minister resigned over a police investigation into a case that began before he took office.

A lawyer, Hanegbi has impeccable right-wing credentials. His mother Geula Cohen was a leading member of the now defunct ultra-nationalist Tehiya party. In 1982, he joined protesters resisting Israel's pullout from the Sinai under a peace deal with Egypt.
But former Likud Prime Minister Yitzhak Shamir in February slammed Hanegbi's abilities, telling the Maariv daily Hanegbi would be unfit for the post "even after 50 years on the job".
PRIME MINISTER'S OFFICE DIRECTOR GENERAL AVIGDOR LIEBERMAN, 39, immigrated to Israel from Russia in 1978 and became involved in Likud party politics while a student at Hebrew University.
The burly Lieberman has a strongman reputation and has long served Netanyahu.

In the course of the police investigation into the current scandal, Lieberman provoked a public outcry when he slammed police as "racist" and said: "Police have become a political weapon, a means of settling scores".

ARYEH DERI, 38, member of parliament from the Shas religious party, is already on trial for corruption and figured at the centre of Israel television allegations that spurred the present scandal and police probe.

Kingmaker Deri has led Shas into both Labour- and Likud-led government coalitions. In 1993, he resigned as interior minister in the Labour government after Israel's High Court ordered then prime minister Yitzhak Rabin to fire him over the indictment that led to his current trial.
